geometry.polygon: vertical column with overhead V (or joined palms)
geometry.summary: From a stable Mountain base, both arms rise overhead on a long line from soles through side ribs to fingertips. Elbows soft, shoulders drop away from ears, ribs stay quiet rather than flared. Palms may face each other, touch lightly, or stay shoulder-width. The polygon is an upright column topped by an open V or a soft diamond of joined hands.

reaction.name: Lift-and-open
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the field shifts from a compact vertical stand toward a lengthened overhead reach, then briefly settles in the quiet at the top of the inhale before return.

breath.lands_in: side ribs and soft upper lungs, then quiet pause at turn
breath.cue: Inhale arms up for 4; soft 1-count pause at the top without strain; exhale arms down or stay up for 4. Never force the pause.

orientation.cue: Crown continues the line of the heels; arms stack over the side body, not behind the ears
orientation.gravity: Even weight on both feet (big toe mound, little toe mound, heel); lift without tipping back
orientation.gaze: Soft toward thumbs or slightly forward-up only if the neck stays free; otherwise gaze soft horizontal
orientation.degrees_hint: 0° torso lean; arms ~180° overhead relative to floor when range allows

attention.primary: The turn of the breath at the top of the inhale (and optionally the bottom of the exhale)

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: As breath moves in and out, rest awareness in the brief inner and outer pauses where the breath turns, without rushing back into the next movement; in that still interval, the nature of awareness is pointed to.
adiyogi.method_summary: Practice: stand or sit with natural breath. Notice the micro-pause after inhale and after exhale. Keep attention in those gaps rather than on forcing the breath. In this door, braid the method with arms overhead so the soft pause at the top of the inhale is easier to feel.

honesty.disclosure: Linking Upward Salute to VBT dharana 002 is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not a claim of ancient one-to-one canon.
honesty.notes: Serial school index pairs D-002 with method index 002. Shared experiential hook (breath-turn awareness) is a teaching braid only; editions also note verse-24/25 clustering as one breath-pause family.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: If standing overhead reach aggravates shoulders or low back, practice the same breath-pause attention seated with arms resting or only partially raised.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Ease range if shoulders, neck, or low back complain; keep ribs soft and avoid forcing arms behind the ears.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door D-002, Upward Salute, Urdhva Hastasana. From a steady stand, both arms rise overhead.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: Feet root like Mountain. Arms lift on one line from heels through side ribs to fingertips. Soft elbows. Shoulders away from ears. Palms face or lightly touch.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Weight even on both feet. Do not tip back. Crown stays over heels. Gaze soft to the thumbs, or forward if the neck prefers.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Inhale four as arms rise. Soft one-count pause at the top. Exhale four. Six easy cycles. Never strain the pause.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Primary lock: the turn of the breath at the top. Secondary: length from soles to fingertips without shrugging.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: Feel the school cue Lift-and-open: compact stand becomes lengthened reach, then a quiet settle in the pause.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: VBT method 002: rest awareness in the brief pause where the breath turns, inside and outside. Notice the gap; do not force it.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Exhale arms down to Mountain, or stay up if steady. Soften shoulders. Keep the pause awareness for one more quiet breath, then release.
